chunks: Ahmad ibn Isha narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awadd and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about a man who divorced his wife, testified to taking her back, but did not have intercourse, then divorced her again in another period of purity in accordance with the Sunnah. Is the second divorce established without intercourse? He said, 'Yes, if he testified to taking her back and did not have intercourse, the divorce is considered the second one.'

key_terms.رَجْعَتُهَا: Revocation of divorce (taking the wife back during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: Does the second divorce count if the husband testified to taking her back but did not have intercourse?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a specific nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of *raj'ah* (revocation) when it occurs without sexual intercourse. It establishes that the second divorce is legally binding and counts towards the limit of three, provided the husband explicitly testifies to the revocation, thereby preventing the wife from returning to him without a new contract (*halala*) after the third divorce. This ruling underscores the importance of verbal declaration and witness testimony in marital law, distinct from the physical act of consummation.
